h1: Fencing in Mesquite, TX: Installation, Repair and Gates
heroSub: Mesquite's older neighborhoods east of Dallas along I-635 and I-30 are full of fences that have outlived their first run. Call now and compare written quotes from independent fence contractors.
introHtml:
Fencing in Mesquite usually starts with an old fence that has finally given up. Many homes east of Dallas along I-635 and I-30 went up in the 1970s through the 1990s, and the original wood fence on a lot of them is leaning, grey and shedding pickets. The real question is rarely whether to act, but whether to repair a section or replace the whole run.

White Rock Fence Co is an advertising site, not a fence contractor. It connects Mesquite homeowners with independent fence contractors who quote the work, and it builds nothing itself. Call now at (214) 555-0137, then compare two or three written quotes. For wider pricing context, see fence costs in Dallas.

services.title: Wood privacy fence installation
services.desc: Cedar or pine privacy fences, including board-on-board, for Mesquite back yards. The City of Mesquite caps rear yard fences at 8 feet, so ask each contractor to quote the exact height you want.

services.title: Fence repair
services.desc: Leaning sections, rotted posts and missing pickets on older Mesquite fences. Ask each contractor to price a repair and a full replacement side by side, because the City's permit rule applies when 50 percent or more of a fence is replaced.

services.title: Gate repair and automatic gates
services.desc: Sagging walk gates, drive gates that drag and openers that quit. Power wiring for a gate opener is electrical work, so ask the installer who holds the electrical license.

services.title: Wrought iron fences
services.desc: Steel and iron-style fences for front yards and side gates. Mesquite limits a front yard fence to 3 1/2 feet with 50 percent through-vision, which an open iron design can meet, so confirm the details with the City.

sections.heading: What the City of Mesquite says about fences
sections.html:
Mesquite's fence rules sit in Chapter 5, Article V of the city's Code of Ordinances. Under Sec. 5-141, a permit is required for any fence over 2 feet in height, for replacing 50 percent or more of a fence, for switching to different materials and for any relocation. The code's wording covers building, replacing, relocating or repairing a fence, so ask the City whether your particular repair needs a permit before work starts.

Heights are in Sec. 5-143. Rear yards can go up to 8 feet, and side yards up to 8 feet as far as the house line, with a corner lot exception: anything over 3.5 feet must be set back 10 feet from the exterior side line. Front yards are limited to 3 1/2 feet with 50 percent through-vision, and Sec. 5-146 bars any fence that interferes with traffic visibility across a corner.

Sec. 5-144 lists chain-link, vinyl, composite, brick, stone, stucco, concrete and wooden pickets as materials, and it prohibits plywood, corrugated steel and fiberglass panels. This page does not list a permit fee or say whether Mesquite registers fence contractors, so ask the City directly. Confirm every rule with the City of Mesquite and your HOA before anything is built.

sections.heading: Replacing a fence from the 1970s to the 1990s
sections.html:
A fence from that era is often on its second or third life. A common complaint is a run that leans after a windstorm or after a dry spell, and much of the Dallas area sits on expansive clay that swells and shrinks with moisture. Ask every contractor how the posts will be set and what is in the quote, rather than expecting one standard answer.

For scale on repairs, one Dallas fence company advertises board replacement at $25 to $60 per board installed and straightening a leaning 10 to 30 foot section at $300 to $800. A different DFW firm advertises $300 to $1,200 for storm damage repair. These are ranges the firms publish, not quotes from this site, and your fence may land outside them.

On replacement, one DFW fence company advertises cedar privacy fence at $18 to $28 per linear foot for standard 6-foot height, while another says board-on-board in Dallas might run $20 to $36 per linear foot. Mesquite allows 8 feet in a rear yard, but no Dallas firm's 8-foot price per foot turned up in our research, so a contractor will have to quote it. See the fence installation and fence repair pages for more.

sections.heading: Gates, iron fencing and quotes you can compare
sections.html:
On gates, one Dallas fence company advertises a gate rebuild at $400 to $1,200, and another DFW firm says problems caught early cost $100 to $300 to fix. Automatic gate prices vary widely from firm to firm, so ask for the gate, the opener and the electrical wiring as separate lines. One DFW firm advertises standard tubular steel fence at $30 to $45 per linear foot installed. More on the gate repair and iron fence pages.

If you live in an HOA, Texas Property Code Sec. 202.023 stops an association from banning a perimeter fence, but it can still regulate the type of fencing, so get written approval first. If a fence on the property line is used by both neighbors, Texas Law Help says both own it and share the repair cost; that is general information, not legal advice. Texas811 says the contractor is responsible for calling 811 two business days before digging.

Texas does not license fence contractors at the state level, and some cities register them, so ask for proof of insurance and for the City's rules on registration. A comparable quote names the height, material, post type, gate hardware and who applies for the City permit. Call now at (214) 555-0137 and get two or three of those in writing. Neighboring Garland has its own city rules, so do not assume they match.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to replace my fence in Mesquite?
faq.a: Per Sec. 5-141 of the City of Mesquite's code, a permit is required for any fence over 2 feet in height, for replacing 50 percent or more of a fence, for changing materials and for any relocation. The same section's wording also mentions repair, so ask the City whether your job counts. Confirm with the City and your HOA before work starts.

faq.q: How tall can a back yard fence be in Mesquite?
faq.a: Sec. 5-143 allows 8 feet in a rear yard, and 8 feet in a side yard as far as the house line. On a corner lot, anything over 3.5 feet must be set back 10 feet from the exterior side line. The front yard limit is 3 1/2 feet with 50 percent through-vision, and your HOA may be stricter, so check both.

faq.q: Should I repair or replace an older Mesquite fence?
faq.a: There is no single rule, and it depends on how many posts have failed. Ask each contractor to price a section repair and a full replacement on the same quote. Remember that replacing 50 percent or more of a fence brings in a City of Mesquite permit.

Texas does not license fence contractors at the state level. Some cities register them, including Dallas, Richardson and Irving, but the Mesquite code pages checked for this site did not say. Ask the City, and ask any contractor for proof of insurance.
